question: With whom did Paul join in greeting the church of God at Corinth and all the saints in Achaia in the opening salutation?
opt1: Timothy our brother
opt2: Sosthenes our companion
opt3: Silas the evangelist
opt4: Titus his fellow helper
correct: Timothy our brother
explanation: Paul identifies Timothy as co-sender in his epistolary salutation to the Corinthian congregation and all believers in Achaia. 2 Corinthians 1:1 (KJV) - "Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Timothy our brother, unto the church of God which is at Corinth, with all the saints which are in all Achaia:"

question: How does the apostle Paul describe God regarding comfort and mercy in 2 Corinthians 1:3?
opt1: The Lord of hosts and sovereign Deliverer of Zion
opt2: The Father of mercies, and the God of all comfort
opt3: The righteous Judge of all living souls
opt4: The shield and exceedingly great reward of the faithful
correct: The Father of mercies, and the God of all comfort
explanation: Paul blesses God as the fountainhead of tender compassions and the divine source of all true consolations. 2 Corinthians 1:3 (KJV) - "Blessed be God, even the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies, and the God of all comfort;"

question: For what divine purpose does God comfort believers in all their tribulation according to 2 Corinthians 1:4?
opt1: That our earthly reputation might be exalted among men
opt2: That we might avoid all future persecutions in the world
opt3: That we may be able to comfort them which are in any trouble
opt4: That we may be preserved from bodily sickness and fatigue
correct: That we may be able to comfort them which are in any trouble
explanation: Believers receive divine solace in order to become empathetic instruments capable of encouraging others with that same consolation. 2 Corinthians 1:4 (KJV) - "Who comforteth us in all our tribulation, that we may be able to comfort them which are in any trouble, by the comfort wherewith we ourselves are comforted of God."

question: What severe experience had Paul and his companions undergone in Asia, having the sentence of death in themselves?
opt1: They were shipwrecked thrice upon the reefs of Melita
opt2: They were cast into the deepest dungeon of Philippi
opt3: They were condemned to fight wild beasts at Ephesus
opt4: We were pressed out of measure, above strength, insomuch that we despaired even of life
correct: We were pressed out of measure, above strength, insomuch that we despaired even of life
explanation: Paul describes an overwhelming crisis in the province of Asia that surpassed human endurance and led them to trust solely in God. 2 Corinthians 1:8 (KJV) - "For we would not, brethren, have you ignorant of our trouble which came to us in Asia, that we were pressed out of measure, above strength, insomuch that we despaired even of life:"

question: Why was the sentence of death placed upon Paul and his companions in Asia according to 2 Corinthians 1:9?
opt1: That we should not trust in ourselves, but in God which raiseth the dead
opt2: That their earthly ministry might quickly come to an end
opt3: That the Roman authorities might show judicial clemency
opt4: That they might seek political asylum in neighboring provinces
correct: That we should not trust in ourselves, but in God which raiseth the dead
explanation: Their extreme peril eliminated all human self-reliance, anchoring their faith exclusively in the resurrection power of God. 2 Corinthians 1:9 (KJV) - "But we had the sentence of death in ourselves, that we should not trust in ourselves, but in God which raiseth the dead:"

question: In what did Paul and his fellow workers rejoice concerning the testimony of their conscience in the world?
opt1: In worldly eloquence and philosophical superiority
opt2: In simplicity and godly sincerity, not with fleshly wisdom
opt3: In extensive genealogical records and ritual purity
opt4: In the commendations received from regional magistrates
correct: In simplicity and godly sincerity, not with fleshly wisdom
explanation: Paul boasted in transparent integrity and divine sincerity rather than worldly rhetorical stratagems or human cleverness. 2 Corinthians 1:12 (KJV) - "For our rejoicing is this, the testimony of our conscience, that in simplicity and godly sincerity, not with fleshly wisdom, but by the grace of God, we have had our conversation in the world, and more abundantly to you-ward."

question: Who were the three preachers mentioned by Paul who preached Jesus Christ among the Corinthians as yea and not nay?
opt1: Peter, Barnabas, and John Mark
opt2: Apollos, Aquila, and Titus
opt3: Paul, Silvanus, and Timotheus
opt4: Stephen, Philip, and Agabus
correct: Paul, Silvanus, and Timotheus
explanation: Paul, Silas (Silvanus), and Timothy consistently proclaimed Christ as the unwavering affirmation of divine truth. 2 Corinthians 1:19 (KJV) - "For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who was preached among you by us, even by me and Silvanus and Timotheus, was not yea and nay, but in him was yea."

question: What affirmation does Paul make concerning all the promises of God in Christ in 2 Corinthians 1:20?
opt1: They remain conditional upon legal perfection under the covenant
opt2: They are postponed until the final restoration of the temple
opt3: They are partially fulfilled through ascetic self-denial
opt4: For all the promises of God in him are yea, and in him Amen
correct: For all the promises of God in him are yea, and in him Amen
explanation: Every divine promise finds its definitive fulfillment and steadfast affirmation in Jesus Christ unto the glory of God. 2 Corinthians 1:20 (KJV) - "For all the promises of God in him are yea, and in him Amen, unto the glory of God by us."

question: What divine guarantee has God given into the hearts of believers according to 2 Corinthians 1:22?
opt1: Who hath also sealed us, and given the earnest of the Spirit in our hearts
opt2: An infallible immunity against physical afflictions and pain
opt3: A written certificate of exemption from imperial decrees
opt4: A miraculous vision guaranteeing financial prosperity on earth
correct: Who hath also sealed us, and given the earnest of the Spirit in our hearts
explanation: God seals His redeemed people and grants the Holy Spirit as an earnest (pledge/down payment) of their ultimate inheritance. 2 Corinthians 1:22 (KJV) - "Who hath also sealed us, and given the earnest of the Spirit in our hearts."

question: Why did Paul state he delayed coming again to Corinth, calling God for a record upon his soul?
opt1: Because he was detained indefinitely by shipwreck at Cenchrea
opt2: To spare you I came not as yet unto Corinth
opt3: Because he lacked sufficient monetary support for the journey
opt4: To avoid facing the civil magistrates of the Achaian court
correct: To spare you I came not as yet unto Corinth
explanation: Paul postponed his visit out of pastoral forbearance, desiring to give them opportunity to correct abuses before arriving in discipline. 2 Corinthians 1:23 (KJV) - "Moreover I call God for a record upon my soul, that to spare you I came not as yet unto Corinth."

question: What resolution did Paul make with himself regarding his next visit to Corinth?
opt1: That he would demand full financial compensation for his labour
opt2: That he would bring an escort of Macedonian elders with him
opt3: That I would not come again to you in heaviness
opt4: That he would dissolve the assembly if they remained divided
correct: That I would not come again to you in heaviness
explanation: Paul resolved not to visit in sorrow or distressing confrontation if pastoral correspondence could restore mutual joy. 2 Corinthians 2:1 (KJV) - "But I determined this with myself, that I would not come again to you in heaviness."

question: With what inward disposition and emotion did Paul write his previous epistle to the Corinthians?
opt1: With theological detachment and cold formal argumentation
opt2: With imperial authority demanding immediate unquestioned submission
opt3: With lighthearted jesting to minimize their congregational errors
opt4: Out of much affliction and anguish of heart I wrote unto you with many tears
correct: Out of much affliction and anguish of heart I wrote unto you with many tears
explanation: Paul's admonitions sprang from deep pastoral sorrow and profound affection rather than punitive vindictiveness. 2 Corinthians 2:4 (KJV) - "For out of much affliction and anguish of heart I wrote unto you with many tears; not that ye should be grieved, but that ye might know the love which I have more abundantly unto you."

question: What pastoral action did Paul urge the church to take toward the repentant offender disciplined by the congregation?
opt1: To forgive him, and comfort him, lest perhaps such a one should be swallowed up with overmuch sorrow
opt2: To banish him permanently from all fellowship and communion
opt3: To impose a severe monetary fine payable to the poor saints
opt4: To require a public fast of forty days before receiving his petition
correct: To forgive him, and comfort him, lest perhaps such a one should be swallowed up with overmuch sorrow
explanation: Restoration and gracious comfort must follow church discipline when the offender genuinely repents, guarding against despair. 2 Corinthians 2:7 (KJV) - "So that contrariwise ye ought rather to forgive him, and comfort him, lest perhaps such a one should be swallowed up with overmuch sorrow."

question: Why was mutual forgiveness and restoration essential among the Corinthians regarding the adversary?
opt1: Lest Roman officials intervene in congregational deliberations
opt2: Lest Satan should get an advantage of us: for we are not ignorant of his devices
opt3: Lest the Jewish synagogues accuse the church of civil disorder
opt4: Lest false teachers claim exclusive apostolic oversight in Achaia
correct: Lest Satan should get an advantage of us: for we are not ignorant of his devices
explanation: Unforgiving hardness in the church provides Satan an opening to fracture communion and destroy vulnerable believers. 2 Corinthians 2:11 (KJV) - "Lest Satan should get an advantage of us: for we are not ignorant of his devices."

question: Why had Paul no rest in his spirit when he arrived in Troas to preach Christ's gospel, though a door was opened unto him?
opt1: Because the silversmiths raised a violent riot against him
opt2: Because he was afflicted with a sudden blinding illness
opt3: Because I found not Titus my brother
opt4: Because imperial soldiers confiscated his travel documents
correct: Because I found not Titus my brother
explanation: Paul's deep concern for the Corinthian situation prevented peace until he could meet Titus and receive their report. 2 Corinthians 2:13 (KJV) - "I had no rest in my spirit, because I found not Titus my brother: but taking my leave of them, I went from thence into Macedonia."

question: For what triumphant leading did Paul offer thanksgiving to God in 2 Corinthians 2:14?
opt1: For granting him great worldly riches through the merchant trade
opt2: For preserving his earthly body from any physical distress
opt3: For delivering all Asia Minor into his political administration
opt4: Which always causeth us to triumph in Christ, and maketh manifest the savour of his knowledge by us in every place
correct: Which always causeth us to triumph in Christ, and maketh manifest the savour of his knowledge by us in every place
explanation: God leads His apostolic messengers in continuous spiritual victory, diffusing the sweet fragrance of gospel knowledge through their ministry. 2 Corinthians 2:14 (KJV) - "Now thanks be unto God, which always causeth us to triumph in Christ, and maketh manifest the savour of his knowledge by us in every place."

question: How does the apostle describe the message of Christ's ministers to those that perish and those that are saved?
opt1: To the one we are the savour of death unto death; and to the other the savour of life unto life
opt2: To the one an earthly proverb of wisdom, and to the other an irrelevant fable
opt3: To both a message of political emancipation from Roman oppression
opt4: To neither a matter of eternal consequence, but of moral instruction
correct: To the one we are the savour of death unto death; and to the other the savour of life unto life
explanation: The gospel produces opposite effects depending on the recipient's spiritual condition: judgment unto death or renewal unto eternal life. 2 Corinthians 2:16 (KJV) - "To the one we are the savour of death unto death; and to the other the savour of life unto life. And who is sufficient for these things?"

question: How does Paul contrast his ministry with the false teachers in 2 Corinthians 2:17?
opt1: We enforce the ceremonial ordinances of Moses with strict oaths
opt2: For we are not as many, which corrupt the word of God: but as of sincerity, but as of God
opt3: We peddle esoteric philosophical doctrines for commercial gain
opt4: We require written letters of recommendation from civic councils
correct: For we are not as many, which corrupt the word of God: but as of sincerity, but as of God
explanation: Paul refuses to adulterate or huckster God's word for profit, preaching with godly integrity as commissioned by God Himself. 2 Corinthians 2:17 (KJV) - "For we are not as many, which corrupt the word of God: but as of sincerity, but as of God, in the sight of God speak we in Christ."

question: What pastoral appeal does Paul make to the Corinthians concerning the disciplined brother in 2 Corinthians 2:8?
opt1: Wherefore deliver him unto Satan for the destruction of the flesh
opt2: Wherefore demand from him a double restitution of silver
opt3: Wherefore I beseech you that ye would confirm your love toward him
opt4: Wherefore banish him from the assembly until the day of redemption
correct: Wherefore I beseech you that ye would confirm your love toward him
explanation: Paul urges the Corinthian church to formally reaffirm their sincere Christian love and fellowship toward the repentant offender. 2 Corinthians 2:8 (KJV) - "Wherefore I beseech you that ye would confirm your love toward him."

question: In whose presence and authority did Paul forgive the repentant offender for the church's sake in 2 Corinthians 2:10?
opt1: By the decree of the high priest of Jerusalem
opt2: Under the judicial authority of the Roman governor
opt3: In accordance with the traditions of the elders of Judea
opt4: For your sakes forgave I it in the person of Christ
correct: For your sakes forgave I it in the person of Christ
explanation: Paul exercised forgiveness as acting directly in the presence, authority, and conscious fellowship of Jesus Christ. 2 Corinthians 2:10 (KJV) - "To whom ye forgive any thing, I forgive also: for if I forgave any thing, to whom I forgave it, for your sakes forgave I it in the person of Christ;"

question: From whom does Paul declare the sufficiency of the apostles proceeds in 2 Corinthians 3:5?
opt1: Not that we are sufficient of ourselves to think any thing as of ourselves; but our sufficiency is of God
opt2: From the comprehensive training received under Greek rhetoricians
opt3: From the prestigious credentials granted by the Sanhedrin
opt4: From natural human ingenuity and persuasive philosophical skills
correct: Not that we are sufficient of ourselves to think any thing as of ourselves; but our sufficiency is of God
explanation: Apostolic competence does not originate in human ability or self-sufficiency, but exclusively in the enabling grace of God. 2 Corinthians 3:5 (KJV) - "Not that we are sufficient of ourselves to think any thing as of ourselves; but our sufficiency is of God;"

question: How does Paul contrast the letter and the Spirit in describing the ministers of the New Testament?
opt1: Both letter and spirit demand equal adherence to ceremonial washings
opt2: Not of the letter, but of the spirit: for the letter killeth, but the spirit giveth life
opt3: The letter pardons transgression, while the spirit imposes legal bonds
opt4: The letter imparts spiritual perfection, while the spirit produces fear
correct: Not of the letter, but of the spirit: for the letter killeth, but the spirit giveth life
explanation: The written legal code apart from grace condemns sinners to death, whereas the Holy Spirit imparts life and power. 2 Corinthians 3:6 (KJV) - "Who also hath made us able ministers of the new testament; not of the letter, but of the spirit: for the letter killeth, but the spirit giveth life."

question: What term does Paul use in 2 Corinthians 3:7 to describe the Old Covenant written and engraven in stones?
opt1: The eternal covenant of unshakable liberty
opt2: The ministry of boundless mercy and perpetual adoption
opt3: The ministration of death, written and engraven in stones
opt4: The heavenly dispensation of angelic reconciliation
correct: The ministration of death, written and engraven in stones
explanation: The Mosaic covenant, though glorious, was a ministration of death because it exposed sin and pronounced condemnation. 2 Corinthians 3:7 (KJV) - "But if the ministration of death, written and engraven in stones, was glorious, so that the children of Israel could not stedfastly behold the face of Moses for the glory of his countenance; which glory was to be done away:"

question: Why could the children of Israel not steadfastly behold the face of Moses at Mount Sinai?
opt1: Because of thick clouds of thunder and darkness around the tent
opt2: Because Moses had grown old and his eyesight was completely dimmed
opt3: Because the elders were forbidden under penalty of death to look upon him
opt4: For the glory of his countenance; which glory was to be done away
correct: For the glory of his countenance; which glory was to be done away
explanation: The transient divine glory reflecting from Moses' face was so radiant that the Israelites could not gaze upon it directly. 2 Corinthians 3:7 (KJV) - "But if the ministration of death, written and engraven in stones, was glorious, so that the children of Israel could not stedfastly behold the face of Moses for the glory of his countenance; which glory was to be done away:"

question: How does the ministration of righteousness compare in glory with the ministration of condemnation?
opt1: Much more doth the ministration of righteousness exceed in glory
opt2: Both ministrations possess precisely identical measures of splendor
opt3: The ministration of condemnation permanently surpasses the new covenant
opt4: The ministration of righteousness possesses no outward glory at all
correct: Much more doth the ministration of righteousness exceed in glory
explanation: The dispensation that imparts justifying righteousness in Christ far surpasses the dispensation of legal condemnation in glory. 2 Corinthians 3:9 (KJV) - "For if the ministration of condemnation be glory, much more doth the ministration of righteousness exceed in glory."

question: Why did Moses put a vail over his face according to 2 Corinthians 3:13?
opt1: To conceal the shame of his physical exhaustion from the elders
opt2: That the children of Israel could not stedfastly look to the end of that which is abolished
opt3: To signify his personal grief over the rebellion in the wilderness
opt4: To conform to traditional Egyptian ceremonial customs
correct: That the children of Israel could not stedfastly look to the end of that which is abolished
explanation: Moses veiled his face so the people would not gaze at the fading away of the temporary, transitional Old Covenant glory. 2 Corinthians 3:13 (KJV) - "And not as Moses, which put a vail over his face, that the children of Israel could not stedfastly look to the end of that which is abolished:"

question: When is the vail that remains upon the hearts of Israel taken away?
opt1: When they rebuild the temple walls in Jerusalem
opt2: When the Sanhedrin authorizes new rabbinic commentaries
opt3: Which vail is done away in Christ: when the heart shall turn to the Lord, the vail shall be taken away
opt4: When the Roman legions depart from the land of Judea
correct: Which vail is done away in Christ: when the heart shall turn to the Lord, the vail shall be taken away
explanation: The spiritual blindness obscuring the meaning of the Old Testament is removed only when the heart turns in faith to Jesus Christ. 2 Corinthians 3:14-16 (KJV) - "But their minds were blinded: for until this day remaineth the same vail untaken away in the reading of the old testament; which vail is done away in Christ. But even unto this day, when Moses is read, the vail is upon their heart. Nevertheless when it shall turn to the Lord, the vail shall be taken away."

question: What divine reality exists wherever the Spirit of the Lord is according to 2 Corinthians 3:17?
opt1: There is rigorous legal bondage to dietary restrictions
opt2: There is permanent silence and cessation of all preaching
opt3: There is fearful expectation of immediate destruction
opt4: Now the Lord is that Spirit: and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty
correct: Now the Lord is that Spirit: and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty
explanation: The presence of the Holy Spirit liberates believers from the veil of blindness, legalistic condemnation, and the fear of death. 2 Corinthians 3:17 (KJV) - "Now the Lord is that Spirit: and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty."

question: Into what are believers transformed as they behold the glory of the Lord with open face as in a glass?
opt1: Changed into the same image from glory to glory, even as by the Spirit of the Lord
opt2: Transformed into physical angels endowed with celestial wings
opt3: Promoted to earthly rulers with administrative authority over nations
opt4: Returned to the primitive state of Adam prior to his creation
correct: Changed into the same image from glory to glory, even as by the Spirit of the Lord
explanation: Contemplating the glory of Christ through the gospel produces progressive moral and spiritual conformity to His divine likeness. 2 Corinthians 3:18 (KJV) - "But we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image from glory to glory, even as by the Spirit of the LORD."

question: What boldness does the apostle say he uses in preaching the gospel of the New Covenant?
opt1: We employ cryptic allegories and esoteric parables
opt2: Seeing then that we have such hope, we use great plainness of speech
opt3: We speak only through accredited philosophical rhetoric
opt4: We conceal the gospel mysteries behind priestly ceremonies
correct: Seeing then that we have such hope, we use great plainness of speech
explanation: Because of the glorious certainty of the New Covenant hope, Paul speaks with open, transparent clarity rather than veiling the truth. 2 Corinthians 3:12 (KJV) - "Seeing then that we have such hope, we use great plainness of speech:"

question: What disgraceful practices did Paul state he and his companions had renounced in their ministry?
opt1: The collection of voluntary alms from Gentile assemblies
opt2: The study of ancient Hebrew genealogies and histories
opt3: Have renounced the hidden things of dishonesty, not walking in craftiness, nor handling the word of God deceitfully
opt4: The public preaching of the cross to uncircumcised listeners
correct: Have renounced the hidden things of dishonesty, not walking in craftiness, nor handling the word of God deceitfully
explanation: Paul avoided secret manipulation, fraudulent compromise, and theological deception, openly commending the truth. 2 Corinthians 4:2 (KJV) - "But have renounced the hidden things of dishonesty, not walking in craftiness, nor handling the word of God deceitfully; but by manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every man's conscience in the sight of God."

question: To whom is the gospel hid when it remains veiled according to 2 Corinthians 4:3?
opt1: It is hid to the unlearned who lack rabbinic schooling
opt2: It is hid to those who fail to recite daily liturgical prayers
opt3: It is hid exclusively to the Gentile magistrates of Rome
opt4: If our gospel be hid, it is hid to them that are lost
correct: If our gospel be hid, it is hid to them that are lost
explanation: The gospel veil does not arise from obscurity in apostolic preaching, but from spiritual blindness in those who reject the truth. 2 Corinthians 4:3 (KJV) - "But if our gospel be hid, it is hid to them that are lost:"

question: Who hath blinded the minds of them which believe not, lest the light of Christ's glorious gospel should shine unto them?
opt1: The god of this world hath blinded the minds of them which believe not
opt2: The council of elders residing in Caesarea
opt3: The philosophical academy established at Athens
opt4: The imperial senate of the city of Rome
correct: The god of this world hath blinded the minds of them which believe not
explanation: Satan, described as 'the god of this world', actively blinds unbelieving minds to keep them from apprehending Christ's glory. 2 Corinthians 4:4 (KJV) - "In whom the god of this world hath blinded the minds of them which believe not, lest the light of the glorious gospel of Christ, who is the image of God, should shine unto them."

question: Whom does Paul declare that the apostles preach, refusing to preach themselves?
opt1: We preach our own apostolic authority and prophetic visions
opt2: For we preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord; and ourselves your servants for Jesus' sake
opt3: We preach civil obedience to Caesar and moral self-reform
opt4: We preach the ceremonial traditions of the elders of Judea
correct: For we preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord; and ourselves your servants for Jesus' sake
explanation: Christ alone is the subject and sovereign Lord of gospel proclamation; apostles are merely humble servants of the church. 2 Corinthians 4:5 (KJV) - "For we preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord; and ourselves your servants for Jesus' sake."

question: What creative act of God did Paul parallel with the illumination of divine knowledge in the face of Jesus Christ?
opt1: The dividing of the Red Sea before the hosts of Israel
opt2: The rain of heavenly manna in the wilderness of Sin
opt3: God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts
opt4: The miraculous sending of quails upon the camp of Israel
correct: God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts
explanation: Just as God summoned physical light at creation, His supernatural power imparts spiritual illumination to regenerate human hearts. 2 Corinthians 4:6 (KJV) - "For God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ."

question: Why does God place the transcendent treasure of the gospel in earthen vessels according to 2 Corinthians 4:7?
opt1: That mortal ministers might achieve great fame among Greek philosophers
opt2: That the vessels might never suffer bodily infirmity or persecution
opt3: That the church might boast in human strength and eloquence
opt4: That the excellency of the power may be of God, and not of us
correct: That the excellency of the power may be of God, and not of us
explanation: Human frailty and mortal weakness serve to demonstrate that the supernatural power of the gospel belongs solely to God. 2 Corinthians 4:7 (KJV) - "But we have this treasure in earthen vessels, that the excellency of the power may be of God, and not of us."

question: How did Paul characterize their apostolic resilience despite suffering extreme hardships in 2 Corinthians 4:8-9?
opt1: Troubled on every side, yet not distressed; we are perplexed, but not in despair; persecuted, but not forsaken; cast down, but not destroyed
opt2: Exempt from every earthly trial and living in perpetual luxury
opt3: Defeated by imperial forces and abandoning our gospel mission
opt4: Seeking armed revolt against the Roman governors of Achaia
correct: Troubled on every side, yet not distressed; we are perplexed, but not in despair; persecuted, but not forsaken; cast down, but not destroyed
explanation: Though battered by severe afflictions on every side, divine preservation prevents the apostles from ever being crushed or abandoned. 2 Corinthians 4:8-9 (KJV) - "We are troubled on every side, yet not distressed; we are perplexed, but not in despair; Persecuted, but not forsaken; cast down, but not destroyed;"

question: What scriptural quote from Psalm 116 did Paul apply to their spirit of faith in 2 Corinthians 4:13?
opt1: The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want
opt2: I believed, and therefore have I spoken; we also believe, and therefore speak
opt3: The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone
opt4: Blessed is he whose transgression is forgiven, whose sin is covered
correct: I believed, and therefore have I spoken; we also believe, and therefore speak
explanation: Unwavering conviction in God's resurrection promises compels gospel ministers to proclaim the truth without fear or hesitation. 2 Corinthians 4:13 (KJV) - "We having the same spirit of faith, according as it is written, I believed, and therefore have I spoken; we also believe, and therefore speak;"

question: What inward transformation occurs even though the outward man perishes through aging and affliction?
opt1: The spirit loses consciousness until the resurrection morning
opt2: The soul experiences progressive deterioration and despair
opt3: Yet the inward man is renewed day by day
opt4: The mind becomes trapped in earthly doubt and uncertainty
correct: Yet the inward man is renewed day by day
explanation: While bodily strength declines under earthly adversity, the believer's inner spiritual life receives daily divine renewal. 2 Corinthians 4:16 (KJV) - "For which cause we faint not; but though our outward man perish, yet the inward man is renewed day by day."

question: What does our light affliction work for us when we look at eternal rather than temporal things?
opt1: A temporary alleviation of tax burdens under Roman decrees
opt2: A prestigious earthly reputation among secular philosophers
opt3: An exemption from facing the judgment seat of Christ
opt4: Worketh for us a far more exceeding and eternal weight of glory
correct: Worketh for us a far more exceeding and eternal weight of glory
explanation: Present transient afflictions bear no comparison to the infinite, enduring weight of celestial glory awaiting the redeemed. 2 Corinthians 4:17 (KJV) - "For our light affliction, which is but for a moment, worketh for us a far more exceeding and eternal weight of glory;"

question: What heavenly reality does the believer anticipate if their earthly house of this tabernacle were dissolved?
opt1: We have a building of God, an house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens
opt2: A return to an ethereal, disembodied spiritual existence forever
opt3: Reincarnation into a purified mortal body upon the earth
opt4: A gilded palace constructed by angels in an earthly paradise
correct: We have a building of God, an house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens
explanation: The mortal physical body is like a temporary tent, but God has prepared an eternal, glorified resurrection body in heaven. 2 Corinthians 5:1 (KJV) - "For we know that if our earthly house of this tabernacle were dissolved, we have a building of God, an house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens."

question: What fundamental principle governs the Christian's present earthly pilgrimage in 2 Corinthians 5:7?
opt1: We walk by rational empiricism and philosophical proofs
opt2: For we walk by faith, not by sight
opt3: We walk by sensory signs and visible miraculous omens
opt4: We walk by legal compliance to ceremonial ordinances
correct: For we walk by faith, not by sight
explanation: Believers order their earthly lives by unwavering trust in God's unseen promises rather than physical appearances. 2 Corinthians 5:7 (KJV) - "(For we walk by faith, not by sight:)"

question: What confident desire does Paul express regarding death and departure from the physical body?
opt1: Desiring to sleep indefinitely in the dust without conscious thought
opt2: Hoping to wander the earth as an unseen guardian spirit
opt3: Willing rather to be absent from the body, and to be present with the Lord
opt4: Seeking to prolong mortal life indefinitely through medical arts
correct: Willing rather to be absent from the body, and to be present with the Lord
explanation: For the believer, physical death immediately ushers the conscious spirit into the presence and fellowship of Jesus Christ. 2 Corinthians 5:8 (KJV) - "We are confident, I say, and willing rather to be absent from the body, and to be present with the Lord."

question: Before what divine tribunal must all believers appear to receive the things done in their body?
opt1: Before the Sanhedrin assembled on Mount Zion
opt2: Before the imperial court of Caesar Augustus
opt3: Before the assembly of patriarchs in the wilderness
